newsitem.title: USA: Mellon to sell corporate trust business.
newsitem.headline: Mellon to sell corporate trust business.

text.p: Mellon Bank Corp said Friday it will seek to sell its corporate trust portfolio business, which has 6,600 accounts worth about $70 billion.
Looking forward, Mellon said it would rather use the funds required to grow that business for other purposes.

"The business is profitable," said Mellon spokesman Jim Dever. "But down the road we realize that in order to be competitive the business will need additional investment that Mellon can dedicate elsewhere."
Dever said that in terms of size, the company's corporate trust portfolio -- with about $70 billion in assets -- was among the top ten corporate trusts businesses in the country.
The company said that the sale would not meterially effect its earnings or its other trust businesses.
"We remain strongly committed to our core trust, master-trust, custody and investment management businesses," Dever said.
Mellon's corporate trust business accounts for less than three percent of the company's overall trust business, which falls under the fee-based business category, according to Dever.
Mellon's fee-based business accounts for about 58 percent of the company's overall revenue, he said.
"The corporate trust business is a business driven by scale," Dever said. "It has to be at a certain magnitude to compete effectively."
